lines.t: This is Apollo control at 56 hours 52 minutes at ground lapse time.
We monitored the pass over to Nana Reeve, which occurred a few moments ago, and at that time there was no calm, no air to ground communication between mission control and the crew.
crew.
The crew evidently is in the process of settling down for their rest cycle and hopefully for a good night's sleep for them or a good period of sleep for them.
We will continue to stand by and watch the circuits.
In the meantime, at 56 hours, 53 minutes, with the spacecraft now heading out over the Indian Ocean, this is Apollo Control.
This is Apollo Control at 57 hours, 50 minutes into the mission.
We've had no new communication, no additional communication with the crew since our last report.
Spacecraft at the present time is on the 37th Rev, flying over crossing South America.

During a recent pass in which the Redstone had acquisition, we received no downlink bioinstrumentation, leading the flight surgeon, Dr. John Ziegelschmitt, to conclude that the crew was probably in the stages of finishing up its light housekeeping preparation for a sleep portion during the rest cycle.

Now, we've maintained a silence here in an effort to permit the crew to have as much rest time as possible after they're having completed a rather busy day checking out the systems on Spider, the LEM spacecraft.
All systems seem to be working well as far as the spacecrafts are concerned.
And at 57 hours, 52 minutes into the flight of Apollo 9, this is Apollo control.
This is Apollo Control at 58 hours, 57 minutes ground elapsed time.
Spacecraft at the present time has been acquired by the tracking station at Hawaii, and we've been observing to see if there was any biomedical data that would be down linked.
This particular time, there is no indication that biomedical data is being down linked.
We'll continue to observe that.
Meanwhile, other data, as far as the spacecraft systems systems are concerned.
Looks good.
The Hawaii station will have the spacecraft for another four or five minutes, and then we'll have about five minutes of acquisition by the tracking ship Redstone.
We'll continue to monitor the systems and come back up if we can.
if there is any significant change.

Well, this is Apollo Control at 59 hours, 15 minutes into the mission.
During the last part of the Hawaii pass and a portion of the Redstone Pass, the flight surgeon received some biomedical information on the command module pilot.
That would have been Dave Scott who was in the right couch.
And the initial indications were that his rates were 60 beats per minute and his respiration was about 20, averaging about 20 per minute.
And during the balance of the pass across the Redstone, those rates were decreasing, leading the flight surgeon to suspect that Dave was in the process of going to sleep, settling down for sleep.
We have not received any biomedical parameters on the other two astronauts.

However, since conversation has been kept to a minimum, no conversation as a matter of fact since early in the flight after Tana Rive following the All three are resting and perhaps the other two are sleeping also.
At 59 hours, 17 minutes, this is Apollo Control.
This is Apollo control at 59 hours, 59 minutes, GET time.
We have some more definitive information on the revised timeline covering the activities on day four, that's tomorrow.
The flight plan is essentially the same up to LEM hatch opening, which is approximately, which occurs approximately 72 hours and 50 minutes at GET.
The hatches will, the hatches in the LEM and the CSM will remain open for approximately one daylight pass during that general timeframe.
Then they will be closed at approximately 74 hours G .E .T.
This closing is about an hour and a half earlier than that in the original flight plan.
During the CSM hatch opening, the command module pilot Dave Scott will attempt to retrieve those thermal samples which are near the CSM hatch, if he can at all possibly do it.
The TV pass that was scheduled for 75 hours G .E .T.
has been moved up slightly.
the Goldstone acquisition will be 74 hours 57 minutes.

And during this time, we expect that the commander will either be in the process of transferring from LM back to command service module, or he will either be actually transferring or we'll be making preparations for it.
This information should be transmitted to us during the TV pass.

During our last transmission at 59 hours 17 minutes, we reported incorrectly that our last previous conversation, or the last previous conversation between MCC and the crew, the Apollo 9 crew, occurred during a pass over Tanana Reeve.
The last conversation between the crew and ground occurred during the ARIA acquisition at 5622, that is from that time frame 5622 to 5632 G .E .T.

At 60 hours and 4 minutes into the flight of Apollo 9 with the spacecraft now over India and with the astronauts in their rest period with one of them fairly well asleep, fairly soundly asleep, this is Apollo Control.
This is Apollo control at 60 hours, 48 minutes, ground elapsed time.
Apollo 9 is over, and the Pacific Ocean at the present time approaching the west coast of South America.
And on this, the 38th Rev, the crew has settled down during this rest cycle.
Biomedical data on the commander Commander and the Command Module Pilot recently was monitored and the information led the surgeon to conclude that the
that's Dave Scott, was soundly asleep while Jim McDevitt, the commander, was resting but perhaps not soundly asleep.
Scott's heart rate was in the low 40s, that is his average heart rate, his mean heart rate, while the commander's heart rate was in the 70s.
The cabin pressure in Apollo 9 is holding steady at 4 .9 pounds per square inch, and the temperature is about 70 degrees Fahrenheit.
All of the systems seem to be functioning well on the spacecraft at this time.
There is a, here meanwhile at Mission Control, there is a beehive of activity with the shifts just about ready to change.
The gold team, which has been on for the past several hours, is about ready to leave, and it will be replaced by the team identified as the orange team.

Apollo 9 is presently just south of Japan.

lines.t: This is Apollo Control, 66 hours, 50 minutes, ground elapsed time.
The crew of Apollo 9 at this time is scheduled to end its sleep period.
We're less than a minute away from acquisition at the tracking ship Mercury in the South Pacific.
There may be problems in communications during this pass.

However, there is a standby high frequency relay available for relaying voice communication back to the mission control center.

Meanwhile, the spacecraft analysis report on systems shows that the cryogenic oxygen and hydrogen for the fuel cells in nominal values, quantities ranging around 75 percent of cryogenic oxygen in both tanks and around 70 percent average on both tanks of hydrogen.
In total weight there are 487 pounds of oxygen in both tanks and 40 pounds of hydrogen.
The fuel cell performance is quite nominal.
The temperatures in the fuel cell are holding very tight limits and the performance all around seems to be quite excellent with no problems.
All the command and service module temperatures are registering along the normal range.
